analysis: The trial succeeded with pinned-host macro validation HR@10 of 0.5237, improving by 0.0275 over the supplied 0.4962 result, 0.0199 over the historical 0.5038 reference, and 0.0187 over the stated SASRec baseline of 0.505. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.550, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.595, Electronics 0.365, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.585. Electronics remains the weakest category; no prior category scores were supplied to establish its improvement. These results support retaining the complete architecture, but cannot isolate preference fusion’s contribution because the attention block was also restored. The supplied code does not implement the planned diagnostic checks. Training allocation was 504.43 GPU-seconds; no test performance was reported.
code_summary: Trains one independent ConvRec per category with eight causal dilated convolutional residual blocks, followed by one pre-normalized two-head causal attention residual with 0.2 dropout. Attention excludes future and padding keys, supplies a safe diagonal for fully masked rows, and zeros padded outputs. A cumulative mean of pre-dropout item embeddings feeds a learned projection and LayerNorm; a channel-wise sigmoid gate interpolates this preference representation with backbone features before final LayerNorm. Gate weights start at zero and bias at -2. Tied item embeddings and a jointly trained item bias score candidates. Training retains 32-negative cross-entropy, random-prefix sampling, AdamW, cosine scheduling, gradient clipping, seed 42, and validation HR@10 checkpoint selection with NDCG tie-breaking and 25-epoch patience. The generated predictor reconstructs the architecture from train.py and metadata, uses shared history packing, and loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category. State loading is strict by PyTorch default, although strict=True is not explicit. No ensemble or checkpoint averaging is used.
